chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Bistam from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

A man said to him, 'May I be your ransom, does a man embrace his brother?' He said, 'Yes. Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was informed on the day Khaybar was conquered that Ja'far had arrived. He said, 'By Allah, I do not know which of the two I am more joyful about: Ja'far's arrival or the conquest of Khaybar.' He said, 'Then Ja'far did not delay before arriving.' He said, 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) rose and embraced him and kissed what was between his eyes.'

The man said to him, 'The four rak'ahs that I have heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) commanded Ja'far (peace be upon him) to pray.' He said, 'When he arrived, peace be upon him, he said to him,

key_terms.قُلْ هُوَ اَللّهُ أَحَدٌ: Say: He is Allah, the One (Quranic surah)

ai.seo_question: What is the method and reward of the four-rak'ah prayer known as Salat al-Tasbih?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the permissibility of male-male embrace through the Prophet’s affectionate greeting of Ja'far ibn Abi Talib, highlighting the emotional weight he placed on his brother's arrival alongside the military victory of Khaybar. It subsequently details the ritual of *Salat al-Tasbih*, a four-rak'ah prayer with a specific dhikr distribution, promising comprehensive forgiveness for sins committed between performances, a practice highly regarded in Shia jurisprudence for its spiritual efficacy.
